subject: Model comparison between multilevel & single level model

messages.author: 3cd60df2fed2c89f
messages.subject: Model comparison between multilevel & single level model
parts:
Hi, I am recently trying to justify my data to fit a single-level LGCM well against a multilevel LGCM. Is that reasonable to conduct chi-squared difference test on them? As the covariance structures for calculating their df seemed different after reading some of the posts here, that multilevel "additionally" introduced a between-level covariance matrix (I am not sure if I got it right) compared to single-level model.

If not, how can I construct models to justify that. Thank you very much.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Model comparison between multilevel & single level model
parts: Is that reasonable to conduct chi-squared difference test on them?

No, the models are not nested.  To test the null hypothesis that there is no cluster-level variance to model, you can fit your single-level model as the Level-1 component of a MLSEM, whose Level-2 component simply fixes all (co)variances to zero.  That model is nested in the MLSEM in which the Level-2 parameters are estimated, so you can conduct a chi-squared difference test.
